questions.explanation: SLA stands for Service Level Agreement.

questions.stem: What is a Service Level Agreement?
options: An internal memo describing IT department goals
A software licence for database products
A contractual agreement between a service provider and a customer outlining the expected level of service, including quality, availability and responsibilities
A technical specification for network hardware
A marketing brochure listing service features
questions.explanation: An SLA is a contractual commitment between a service provider and a customer that outlines the level of service expected, including quality, availability and responsibilities.

questions.stem: A guarantee of 99.9% uptime for a cloud-based data storage service is an example of which SLA aspect?
questions.explanation: Availability defines the agreed level of uptime for a data service; 99.9% uptime is the given example.

questions.stem: A commitment that support tickets will be addressed within 24 hours relates to which SLA aspect?
questions.explanation: Response time outlines the time frame within which the provider commits to respond to queries, issues or requests.

questions.stem: Which SLA aspect addresses encryption, access controls and adherence to data protection laws?
questions.explanation: Data security and privacy covers the security measures protecting data and adherence to privacy regulations, such as encryption and access controls.

questions.stem: What does the scalability aspect of an SLA define?
options: The penalties for missing service targets
How the service will scale to accommodate increased data volumes or user demands
The expected accuracy of the data
The conditions for ending the agreement
questions.explanation: Scalability defines how the service will scale to accommodate increased data volumes or user demands, such as procedures for scaling resources under higher loads.

questions.stem: A provision for daily backups and restoring data within 48 hours after a failure is an example of which SLA aspect?
questions.explanation: Data backup and recovery outlines procedures for regular backups and the expected timeframe for recovery in case of a failure.

questions.stem: Which regulation is given as an example of what a healthcare data management SLA might require compliance with?
questions.explanation: The compliance example is a healthcare data management system whose SLA specifies compliance with healthcare privacy regulations such as HIPAA.

questions.stem: What does the termination and penalties aspect of an SLA cover?
options: The uptime percentage of the service
The encryption standards applied to data
The accuracy and reliability of data
The conditions under which either party can end the agreement, and possible penalties for non-compliance
questions.explanation: Termination and penalties outlines when either party can terminate the agreement and may include penalties for non-compliance, such as consistently missing service levels.

questions.stem: Why are Service Level Agreements described as crucial?
options: They establish clear expectations and accountability between providers and customers, helping ensure data services meet defined standards
They eliminate the need for data backups
They guarantee that no system failure will ever occur
They replace the need for security controls
They set the price of cloud storage across the industry
questions.explanation: SLAs establish clear expectations and accountability between service providers and customers so that data services meet defined standards.
